- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (sentiment > 0.0).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or is low (sentiment < 0.0), particularly after recent highs.  
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecasts by applying a 3–5 day moving average to sentiment-weighted price adjustments.  
- Avoid sharp upward revisions after a 3–5 day downtrend; model often overshoots recovery, especially if sentiment is weak.  
- When sentiment is consistently near zero or negative, reduce forecast volatility and shift toward mean-reversion targets from prior 10–15 day range.  
- For horizon > 14 days, model tends to overestimate price stability; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 7-day interval if sentiment is flat or negative.
